blocks.h: What a case study on this page proves
body: A case study is evidence only if your engineers can check it. Each one opens with a profile: segment, province, system, capacity, grade, standards and timeline. Every figure carries its unit, reference temperature, method, sampling point, number of samples and the executed report it comes from: FAT, site acceptance test (SAT), or installation, operational or performance qualification (IQ, OQ, PQ).

We name a client only with written permission; otherwise by segment and province. A second engineer checks every figure against its report, then the client's quality unit approves the text. Deviations raised at FAT and SAT are stated with how each was closed, because a record with no deviations is the one an auditor trusts least.

blocks.h: Questions engineering and quality teams ask

items.q: Why are there no named clients on this page?
items.a: Many pharmaceutical and biotech clients do not allow suppliers to name them, and we publish a case study only with written approval and a signed report behind every figure. Where a client cannot be named, the case study describes it by segment and province. A reference call can go further than a public page, because the client speaks for itself.

items.q: Can we speak to a client in our segment?
items.a: Ask, and say which system and grade you are buying. We can offer [reference segments and systems, and how many]. If no reference matches your segment, we say so and offer the closest system match instead.

items.q: Are the figures from your tests or from the client?
items.a: FAT figures are ours, measured in our test bay on its feed water. SAT and OQ figures are measured on your feed water at your site, against protocols your quality unit approved. PQ data belongs to the client and is published only with its approval, labelled as client data. Each figure names the report it comes from.

items.q: Can we witness another client's FAT?
items.a: Only with that client's permission, and usually under a non-disclosure agreement. [witnessing other clients' FATs: offered, terms] If none can be arranged, we walk you through a redacted FAT protocol and report, and you witness your own FAT against a protocol you approved.

items.q: Will our project become a case study?
items.a: Only if you agree in writing. Your quality unit approves the text and the figures, decides whether you are named, and can withdraw approval later. Nothing confidential to your process, such as product names or batch data, appears on the page.

items.q: Why do you report non-condensable gases in mL per 100 mL, not as a percentage?
items.a: Because EN 285 states the limit that way: no more than 3.5 mL of non-condensable gas per 100 mL of condensate. Reporting the measured volumes, with dryness value and superheat, lets your validation team compare the result with the standard and with your sterilizer's own EN 285 report without a conversion.

items.q: Does a passed FAT mean the system meets USP?
items.a: No. A FAT proves function before shipment: alarms, interlocks, sanitization and controls. Water quality at your points of use is proven on your feed water at SAT and OQ and over PQ. A case study states which milestone it reached, so a FAT result is never presented as a qualified system.
